name: Cell Division — Draft Interface
description: Fig 10.1 (panel b) — division as a compositional rewrite. A prokaryotic cell replicates its chromosome (DNAReplication), segregates the copies toward the two poles (SegregateChromosome), and then splits — an event-driven graph rewrite (Divide) — partitioning state (DNA, biomass) into two daughters and incrementing the cell count. The daughters live as sibling stores under the shared environment, each re-coupling its own interface to it: division does not sever the coupling, it partitions the composition while the daughters remain coupled through the shared environment. All DRAFT processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no dynamics (division/segregation described as event rewrites in the contracts, not implemented).
